solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lake in very good Somerset location for fish

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good or devout
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
Chard is a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A lake in a virtuous corner of Somerset is recommended as a fishing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go PI, then L, then CHARD; 'in' only joins the lake to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, the adult sardine, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Walk about island to the north — mountain top here?

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word for walk is written backwards

parts.note: to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: A walker circles an island and wonders whether the summit lies up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses PACE to ECAP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent covering of ice is what you might expect to find on a high peak, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sorceress left out of ring

indicators.note: left out of means the letter for left is dropped from the word for ring

parts.note: a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A witch has been excluded from the circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey the enchantress who turned Odysseus's men into pigs.

clue.text: Tries somehow to interrupt a member of the family making pronouncement

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the scrambled letters sit inside the family member

parts.note: a son is a family member

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of tries are arranged in some new way

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to butt in on a relative who is making a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of 'Tries'; 'to interrupt' puts them inside the family member, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm declaration or claim is a statement made confidently, a pronouncement.

clue.text: Hellish situation — nurse is swell

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, and the city of hell in Dante
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a nurse remarks that everything is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like the American adjective for great, but it is the verb to bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to enlarge from internal pressure, i.e. to swell as a verb.

clue.text: Game you set about after drink

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the drink

parts.note: hock is German white wine

indicators.note: set about here means turned round, so the old word for you is written backwards

parts.note: ye is the old word for you

explanation.surface: An invitation to get going on a game once the drinks are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck.

clue.text: Cries when there is fire, first to last

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end of the word for fire

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: People scream when a blaze breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls and car horns make loud calls of this kind, as do jeering audiences.

clue.text: Mad man in church, right type to distract congregation?

indicators.note: in puts the mad man inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A lunatic in church is just the sort to disturb worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks incessantly would disturb a worshipping crowd, so it is a playful description.

clue.text: See me getting upset, unwell, communicating via computer

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word me is read backwards

parts.note: ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone frets that they are distressed and poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' merely introduces the clue; 'getting upset' turns ME to EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending electronic messages is a way of corresponding through a computer.

clue.text: English county accommodating a Scottish football team

indicators.note: accommodating means holding within, so A goes inside the county

parts.note: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: An English county is hosting a club from north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart of Midlothian, the Edinburgh football club, is commonly known by this short name.

clue.text: One has got on unexpectedly

parts.note: seems to describe surprising success, but describes a person who boards a ship or plane in secret

explanation.surface: Someone has prospered against the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden passenger travels without a ticket, having boarded without anyone expecting them.

clue.text: Provision for the infirm at no cost? That could make one happy-go-lucky

parts.note: care is looking after the sick
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Free health care for the sick would cheer anyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untroubled and easygoing takes life lightly, without worries.

clue.text: Put down roots in beastly home with the French

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone establishes themselves in an animal's lair alongside the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a permanent home somewhere is to establish yourself there, an idiom of planting.

clue.text: Fulfilling certain female role, nice girl had become agitated about boy initially

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the initial
become agitated says the preceding words are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of boy

explanation.surface: A young woman became upset about a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become agitated' rearranges NICE GIRL HAD into CHILDEARING; 'about' puts that round the B that 'initially' takes from boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying and giving birth to babies is a specifically female biological function.

clue.text: Larking about in underground activity? Nothing right in that

indicators.note: in places the letters for nothing and right inside the pothole sport

parts.note: caving is exploring caves, a sport done below ground
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is fooling around while exploring caves wrong?
explanation.definitionFit: Prancing and frolicking playfully, which is what larking about means.

clue.text: Unfinished building complex in which to find this person's café

indicators.note: in which to find signals that the setter's possessive sits inside the shortened estate
unfinished drops the last letter of the word for building complex

parts.note: an estate is a housing development
the setter refers to themselves, so this person's is mine

explanation.surface: A half-built development where the setter keeps a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims the final E; 'in which to find' then puts the setter's possessive inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French bar or bistro, a word familiar from First World War soldiers in France.

clue.text: Period after St David's Day by the sea

indicators.note: after puts the period behind the date

parts.note: the Welsh patron saint's day is 1 March, written MAR I
a period is a time

explanation.surface: Something happens following Wales's national day at the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is patron saint of Wales; his day is 1 March, rendered MAR plus Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal or connected with the ocean, as a seaside region is described.

clue.text: Man got a lever working, device in physics lab?

indicators.note: working means put into operation, here rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A lab technician pulled a lever to operate apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument for detecting and measuring small electric currents, standard school laboratory kit.

clue.text: Male beast upset at least twenty different animals

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
tens in the plural means at least two tens, so twenty or more

explanation.surface: An overturned male animal annoys a score or more of other creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Weasel-family mammals such as the pine and stone varieties, so several kinds of beast.

clue.text: Prosperity that comes with breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters so they reform in a new order

explanation.surface: Crime pays: riches follow from lawbreaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches and affluence, a plain synonym of being prosperous.

clue.text: Like prominent cleric in US university meeting socialist

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
red is used for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A senior churchman at an American college meets a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops wear a tall pointed hat, so one wearing it is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Party individual — Lorna?

parts.note: a do is a party
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A party of one person, perhaps named Lorna.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel set on Exmoor, so this is her surname.

clue.text: Hiding in grass, chief stayed put

indicators.note: hiding in means concealed within, so the chief word goes inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
main means chief

explanation.surface: A leader concealed in the long grass did not move.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed and not left a place; the verb in its past tense matches.

clue.text: William bicycles — feet getting stuck

indicators.note: getting stuck suggests the letters are lodged within the phrase William bicycles

explanation.surface: William's feet get caught while cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the metrical foot of one short and one long syllable, so poetic feet.

clue.text: Rubbery stuff in cake — I only half lick the content

indicators.note: in places the I and half of lick inside the cake

parts.note: a scone is a small cake

indicators.note: only half keeps the first two of the four letters of lick

explanation.surface: Someone finds rubbery stuff in their cake and only half-licks the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer used for sealants and flexible moulds, rubbery in texture.

clue.text: That is upsetting laymen

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Something disturbs non-clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to introduce a specification, equivalent to i.e. or that is to say.

clue.text: Group in the distance at sea

definitions.meaning: an association of clubs or nations, as in football or a political alliance
an old measure of about three miles, used at sea

explanation.surface: A cluster seen far off over the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a sporting or political alliance, and an old unit of length, about three nautical miles.

clue.text: Opportunity of seeing around Italy taking time? Don't think of leaving

indicators.note: around wraps the word for seeing round the other pieces

parts.note: sight is the chance or faculty of seeing
IT is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: Sightseeing in Italy takes so long you won't want to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay where you are and do nothing, so don't move off.
